title: Swedish Pomerania
capsule: Swedish Pomerania (Swedish: Svenska Pommern) was a Baltic coastal territory held by Sweden from 1630, when Gustavus Adolphus landed at Peenemünde at the start of Sweden's intervention in the Thirty Years' War, through the Peace of Westphalia (1648), which formally awarded Sweden Western Pomerania including Stettin (Szczecin) and the islands of Rügen and Usedom. The territory served as Sweden's strategic foothold in the Holy Roman Empire and a key base for Baltic power projection. Following successive losses in the Great Northern War and the Napoleonic period, Sweden ceded the remaining enclave (Swedish Vorpommern) to Prussia in 1815 by the Congress of Vienna settlement, in exchange for Norway. The territory is now part of the German state of Mecklenburg-Vorpommern.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Borders are well attested through the Peace of Westphalia and subsequent treaties, with clearly demarcated boundaries changing at key diplomatic settlements; the territory is among the better-documented Swedish imperial possessions.
